name: edgar
title: SEC EDGAR — Company Tickers
description: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission's company-tickers file from its EDGAR system: one row per ticker symbol, with the Central Index Key (CIK), EDGAR conformed company name and exchange it is associated with. A company with several listed securities has several rows — 1RT Acquisition Corp. (CIK 2054272) has ONCH, ONCHU and ONCHW — so CIK alone is not a key. The SEC updates the file to support EDGAR searches and does not guarantee its accuracy or scope: it is a ticker list, not a register of every company with securities registered with the SEC.

cik.description: SEC EDGAR Central Index Key — the registrant's identifier in EDGAR, stored as an integer. Unpadded: no leading zeros are stored and none are implied, so the decimal rendering of this column is the CIK. The SEC renders a CIK zero-padded in URLs and filenames (`CIK0000320193`); that is a rendering convention applied to the identifier, not the value the company-tickers file this column is built from carries, and the Parquet column is a signed 64-bit integer. Join it to `edgar_gleif.key` by rendering it as text — see that package's `x-joins`.

company_name.description: Legal name of the registrant as carried in the SEC company-tickers file. The type on this field is declared, not inferred: `nominations.finetype.json` beside this descriptor nominates `representation.text.entity_name` and says why, so the field carries `x-finetype-nominated` and no confidence. Inferred, the label is a draw: finetype returned it on 572 of 600 independent 100-value samples of this column and one of four other types on the rest.

ticker.description: Exchange ticker symbol for the registrant's security.

exchange.description: Listing venue for the ticker (e.g. NYSE, Nasdaq, CBOE, OTC, TXSE — the Texas Stock Exchange).

corpus.description: Lowercased, accent-stripped concatenation of name + ticker + exchange — a derived free-text search field, not a source attribute. The type on this field is declared, not inferred: `nominations.finetype.json` beside this descriptor nominates `representation.text.plain_text` and says why, so the field carries `x-finetype-nominated` and no confidence. Inferred, the label is a draw: finetype returned it on 484 of 600 independent 100-value samples of this column, `unknown` on 97 and one of seven other types on the rest.
